les: Vyf maniere om kos te kry
kaps_punt: Maniere waarop mense hul voedsel verkry - koop; verbou; versamel, visvang, jag

items.bewering: Elke mens het elke dag kos nodig, maar nie almal kry hul kos op dieselfde manier nie.
items.bron: Medical News Today, 'How long can you go without food?' (medicalnewstoday.com): the body keeps only a small energy reserve (glycogen, then fat and protein), so regular eating is needed for normal function. Survival without food runs to weeks, so the sentence is true as a statement about staying healthy, not about survival. That is the natural reading for a Grade 4 learner. The second clause is supported by the Stats SA GHS and food-source items below.

items.bewering: Daar is vyf belangrike maniere waarop mense aan kos kom. Hulle koop dit, of hulle verbou dit self. Hulle kan dit ook versamel, vis vang of jag.
items.bron: The CAPS bullet in the lesson's own kaps_punt names these five, and each is confirmed separately below. The sentence says 'belangrike', not 'die enigste', so it does not claim the list is complete. An observation, not a finding: keeping animals for food (chickens, goats, cattle), which the Stats SA GHS counts as agricultural activity, fits none of the five as this lesson defines them, because 'Verbou' is defined as planting only. Nothing in the lesson claims the five are exhaustive, so this is an omission and not a falsehood.

items.bewering: Die meeste mense in Suid-Afrika koop hul kos by 'n winkel.
items.bron: Stats SA General Household Survey 2023, as reported by ECR (ecr.co.za, 'Quarter of SA households lack access to adequate food'): 11.7% of households named small-scale agriculture as their main source of food. A Nutrition Reviews paper (PMC7948081) says purchases are thought to make up 'the vast majority' of household food in South Africa because own production is low. Retail surveys (BusinessTech) put supermarket use at 83% and spaza-shop use at 45%. 'Die meeste' is a majority claim and is well supported. Spaza shops count as shops; street vendors and fresh-produce markets are the exceptions, and they do not threaten the majority.

items.bewering: Die winkel koop die kos weer by boere en ander mense wat kos maak.
items.bron: Shoprite Holdings, Freshmark (shoprite.co.za): its fresh-produce arm buys directly from local producers. UP / Farmer's Weekly work on fresh-produce markets confirms that supermarkets increasingly buy straight from farmers. Wholesalers and municipal markets in between are left out, which is an acceptable simplification at Grade 4: the sentence says where the food comes from, not every step.

items.bewering: Dink aan 'n brood op die winkelrak. Die winkel het die brood by 'n bakkery gekoop. Die bakker het dit van meel gebak. Die meel kom van koring wat 'n boer geplant het.
items.bron: NAMC wheat food value chain report (namc.co.za) and Farming Portal, 'Inside South Africa's wheat milling industry': the chain runs wheat farmer, then mill (white, brown and cake flour), then bakery (about 80% of SA bread comes from six baking groups), then retail. The order in the lesson is right. Leaving out the mill is fine because 'kom van' is true. Some wheat is imported, but a farmer still planted it, so the sentence holds.

items.bewering: So begin baie van die kos wat ons koop, by 'n boer.
items.bron: Follows from the supply-chain sources above (Freshmark; NAMC wheat value chain). 'Baie' rather than 'alle' is the right quantifier, because bought fish, for example, does not start with a farmer.

items.bewering: Verbou beteken dat jy die kos self kweek.
items.bron: SAWIS trilingual dictionary (sawis.co.za) pairs 'cultivate' with 'verbou'. Grain SA's Afrikaans Pula Imvula and weet.co.za use 'verbou' for growing crops ('mielies wat in Suid-Afrika verbou word'). I could not open the WAT or HAT entry itself, so this rests on established usage sources, which agree.

items.bewering: Hulle plant groente, vrugte of kruie in 'n tuin en gee dit water. By verbou plant die mens self die plante in die grond en sorg vir hulle tot hulle kos gee.
items.bron: Stats SA GHS food-production data (ECR; Polity, 'The quiet erosion: what has happened to subsistence farming in South Africa', 28 Sep 2026): household gardens grow vegetables and fruit for home use. The description of cultivation (plant, water, tend until harvest) is accurate.

items.bewering: Versamel is anders as verbou. 'n Kosversamelaar plant niks nie maar haal kos wat reeds in die natuur groei. Dit kan wilde blare of vrugte wees wat vanself in die veld groei.
items.bron: University of Pretoria MSc dissertation, 'The role and production of traditional leafy vegetables in three rural communities in South Africa' (repository.up.ac.za/handle/2263/28245), and Vorster et al. (ajfand.net): morogo / imifino are wild leafy plants gathered rather than planted, often from fields and fallow land, and eaten in rural South Africa. The contrast with growing your own food is correct.

items.bewering: Sommige plante, bessies en sampioene is giftig.
items.bron: Farmer's Weekly, 'Syringa berries are highly toxic' (farmersweekly.co.za): syringa berries are toxic to children in South Africa. Cape Argus, 7 Jul 2026, quoting the Tygerberg Poisons Information Centre on death cap mushrooms in the Western Cape. The list keeps mushrooms separate from plants, which is correct, because fungi are not plants.

items.bewering: Dit beteken dat hulle mense of diere siek kan maak of skade kan doen as hulle in die liggaam kom, soos wanneer hulle geëet word.
items.bron: Wiktionary 'gif' (Afrikaans: poison, a poisonous substance). DSAE entries 'gifboom' and 'gifblaar' (dsae.co.za): plants harmful to people and livestock. 'As hulle in die liggaam kom' covers eating and also a bite or sting, so it fits both senses of Afrikaans 'giftig' (poisonous and venomous).

items.bewering: 'n Giftige bessie kan amper net so lyk soos een wat veilig is.
items.bron: National Capital Poison Center, 'Pokeberries and grapes look alike' and 'Fall berries only look edible' (poison.org); Children's Hospital of Philadelphia Poison Control Center, 'Poisonous berries' (chop.edu): some poisonous berries closely resemble edible ones. For the parallel case of mushrooms, the Tygerberg Poisons Information Centre (Cape Argus, 7 Jul 2026) says you cannot tell whether one is safe from how it looks.

items.bewering: Daarom moet iemand wat kos versamel, die plante baie goed ken.
items.bron: Poison-centre guidance (poison.org; chop.edu): never eat a wild berry without certain identification by someone who knows the plants. Tygerberg Poisons Information Centre (Cape Argus) gives the same warning for mushrooms. The safety advice is sound.

items.bewering: Mense vang ook vis vir kos. Party vang vis in die see met 'n hengel van die rotse af.
items.bron: 'A survey of the recreational rock angling fishery at Port Elizabeth on the east coast of South Africa' (figshare.utas.edu.au), and Afrikaans South Coast news reporting on 'kushengel' and 'hengelaars' (George Herald; Mosselbaai Advertiser): fishing from the rocks with a rod is a well-established practice in SA. 'Hengel' as the noun for fishing rod: confirmed for the Dutch cognate (Interglot; DBNL), and the Afrikaans compounds 'hengelaar' and 'kushengel' are in active use. I found no Afrikaans dictionary entry online.

items.bewering: Ander gaan met 'n boot uit en vang vis met nette.
items.bron: FAO fishery country profile for South Africa (fao.org, FI_CP_ZA.pdf): SA's offshore sector is dominated by hake trawl and the small-pelagic purse-seine fishery for sardine and anchovy. Both use nets from boats. The sentence does not claim that all boat fishing uses nets, so the linefish handline fishery does not contradict it.

items.bewering: Mense vang ook vis in riviere en damme.
items.bron: Rhodes University, 'An analysis of inland fisheries resource use in the Eastern Cape, South Africa' (researchrepository.ru.ac.za/handle/123456789/5079): subsistence angling in rural dams, with the fish eaten at home. SAIAB, 'Tackling food insecurity through inland fisheries in Limpopo' (saiab.ac.za, 2025).

items.bewering: Daar is die water gewoonlik varswater, wat baie min sout bevat.
items.bron: USGS, 'Surface water use' (usgs.gov): fresh water is water with less than 1 000 mg/L dissolved solids, against roughly 35 g/L for seawater. Rivers and reservoirs are the standard examples. 'Gewoonlik' rightly allows for estuaries and saline inland waters.

items.bewering: Sommige mense jag ook wilde diere vir hul vleis.
items.bron: North-West University, 'Hunting is a multi-billion Rand business' (news.nwu.ac.za): about 200 000 biltong hunters in SA, and 54% hunt for other people as well. DSAE entry 'biltong' (dsae.co.za): dried game meat. 'Sommige' is the right quantifier.

items.bewering: Versamel, visvang en jag haal kos direk uit die natuur. Jy kweek die kos self wanneer jy verbou. Iemand anders het dit gewoonlik eers vir jou gekweek of gevang wanneer jy koop.
items.blok: Uit die natuur of by die winkel
items.bron: Follows from the sources for each method above: UP leafy-vegetable dissertation (gathering), FAO SA fishery profile and Rhodes inland-fisheries study (fishing), NWU on hunting, and Freshmark / NAMC (bought food grown by producers). 'Vang' excludes farmed fish, so 'direk uit die natuur' holds. 'Gekweek' for bought meat and eggs: the Dutch cognate 'kweken' is used for raising animals as well as plants ('forel kweken'), and the sentence's 'gewoonlik' hedges anything that is neither, such as salt. I found no false contrast in the three-way split.

items.bewering: Die meeste mense in Suid-Afrika kry hul kos deur dit te koop.
items.blok: Uit die natuur of by die winkel
items.bron: Same evidence as the first 'die meeste' claim: Stats SA GHS 2023 (ECR, 11.7% of households rely mainly on own agriculture) and Nutrition Reviews (PMC7948081, purchases make up the vast majority of household food). This one is broader than the first ('deur dit te koop', not 'by 'n winkel'), so it is at least as well supported.

items.bewering: kosversamelaar: Iemand wat kos haal wat vanself in die natuur groei, soos wilde blare en vrugte.
items.bron: Consistent with the gathering sources (UP dissertation on wild leafy vegetables, repository.up.ac.za/handle/2263/28245). Read on its own, the definition is true: it describes someone who collects food that grows wild rather than planting it.

items.bewering: giftig: Iets wat mense of diere siek kan maak of skade kan doen as dit in die liggaam kom, soos wanneer dit geëet word.
items.bron: Wiktionary 'gif' (Afrikaans: poison); DSAE 'gifboom' and 'gifblaar' (harmful to people and animals). Read on its own, the definition is accurate and covers both the poisonous and venomous senses of 'giftig'.

opsomming: All 22 claims are confirmed and the lesson has no analogies; the two 'die meeste' superlatives are well supported by Stats SA's household survey, and the only thing worth a person's eye is an omission, not an error: keeping animals for food fits none of the five ways as the lesson defines them, which the lesson never claims to be complete.
